closureReasoning.1-existingContexts: The old loop is replaced by three separated direct calls on the restricted runtime connection. _direct_context asserts current_user equals the runtime login, inv_kernel membership and no super/BYPASSRLS. In the missing-subject case (tenant A, valid epoch) the helper asserts that the epoch matches inv.control_epoch and that tenant_controls is NOT killed before the call, then expects exactly 'Verified service context required'. In the cross-tenant case, the owner first upserts a non-killed tenant_controls row for the other tenant and the same admission asserts run under inv.tenant_id=other; the test then expects exactly 'Current project permission required'. Missing epoch expects 'Current epoch and tenant admission required'. Each case asserts sqlstate 42501, the exact message_primary, and owner-counted (superuser/BYPASSRLS, all-tenant) unchanged counts of workloads, inv.runs, public.runs, business_runs, outbox and idempotency. An epoch failure therefore cannot masquerade as either intended denial, and deleting the subject guard would surface the different project-permission message.
closureReasoning.2-intentHelper: inv.append_first_workspace_intent is now called directly on the runtime role with SQL-supplied Jsonb/sha/canonical, bypassing validate_contract/_validate/HTTP. The positive control (same fixture recipe and valid context) inserts and reads back (spec, digest, version 1) inside force_rollback, and the owner counts are unchanged afterwards. This proves the baseline passes every guard, so each negative differs by exactly one property. 11 intent negatives: gpu1 -> 'Bounded CPU resources required'; cpu501 and memory8388607 -> 'CPU resource bounds exceeded'; extra key workspaceStart, sha mismatch, canonical/spec mismatch (SHA consistent with the changed canonical) and spec tenantId=other -> 'Closed canonical CPU metadata required'; non-ready and stale-version Workspace -> 'Current selected ready Workspace required'; non-member and disabled target -> 'Selected target membership differs'. Shape/resource/target/tenant mutations recompute both canonical text and SHA, so a digest error cannot hide those guards. Owner-side state changes are restored in finally. I confirmed that public.workspaces has no trigger altering version, so the not-ready case changes status alone.
closureReasoning.3-runHelper: The run positive control uses an intent created through the production API, then direct append_first_workspace_run on the runtime role with valid context. It asserts the inv.runs (draft,1,0), public.runs (workspace, workload, draft) and inv.business_runs (project, workspace) rows inside force_rollback, and unchanged owner counts after. 4 run negatives (workspace version+1, workload version+1, sha mismatch, workspace provisioning) each expect exactly 'Current selected intent required' under otherwise valid context with real canonical bytes. The earlier context guards pass, as the positive control demonstrates, so no unrelated missing context/permission/ID blocks them. The inherited 35 cases are retained unchanged (only the loop hunk changed); no skip/xfail/blanket catch was added (grep). The tenant_controls upsert targets the per-test fresh other-tenant UUID, and owner mutations are restored, so there is no cross-test contamination.

The module has 52 cases = 35 inherited + 17 new, and Core is 9469 pass / 46 skip = 9452 + 17. Mutation sensitivity is reasoned from setup and assertions, NOT executed: deleting any single intended predicate (gpu, cpu, memory, closed key set, sha, canonical equality, spec tenant, workspace status, workspace version, membership/enabled, run workspace/workload version, run sha, run status) leaves every other guard passing for that case's single mutation. The call then either reaches INSERT (pytest.raises fails with DID NOT RAISE) or fails with a different type/message, so the exact-message and count assertions detect it. Two cases rely on another layer: if the explicit tenant predicate in the project_grants lookup were deleted, the PUBLIC tenant_isolation RLS on inv.* would still refuse with the same message. That is defense in depth for the same property, not a gap. The code matches my original boundedFix items (a), (b) and (c), with a run sha case beyond them.
